trust_decision.summary: XORMappedAddress.GetFromAs trusts that the attribute value slice is long enough to read the 2-byte family field at xoraddr.go:94; the existing 'len(value) <= 4' guard sits after that read (xoraddr.go:114-116) and only bounds len, while a Go slice expression value[0:2] panics when cap(value) < 2, which is produced by Message.Decode aliasing the value to the end of a buffer whose cap == len (message.go:467).

landing_point.why: An engineer reading only 'panic parsing a malformed XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS' opens XORMappedAddress.GetFromAs and lands on the first byte read of the value; the misplaced length guard is 20 lines below at xoraddr.go:114.

fix_sites.entry_point: (*XORMappedAddress).GetFromAs (public, attr-type parameterised: XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS plus TURN XOR-PEER-ADDRESS/XOR-RELAYED-ADDRESS); (*XORMappedAddress).GetFrom at xoraddr.go:150 is its one-line alias with the same body
fix_sites.module_kind: public library API (attribute decoder, package github.com/pion/stun/v3)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: none: the mirror decoder addr.go:67-98 (MAPPED-ADDRESS/ALTERNATE-SERVER/OTHER-ADDRESS/RESPONSE-ORIGIN) already guards before the read at addr.go:72-75; errorcode.go:58-75, uattrs.go:55-72, fingerprint.go:59-72, textattrs.go:126-134 and integrity.go:98-127 were checked and are guarded

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A value longer than 4 bytes is already 'long enough' for the family field and CheckOverflow bounds it from above, so partially-decoded IPs for 5-19 byte values are a separate decoding concern rather than the reported panic.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Zero-copy attribute values: m.Get returns a slice aliasing m.Raw under the documented contract that it is valid only until Message.Raw changes, so a fix that copies values inside Decode to avoid the tight-cap case breaks the documented zero-allocation hot path and its 0-alloc benchmarks.

O6_input_shapes: zero-length XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS value at the end of a buffer whose cap == len
value slice with cap < 2 so the family field cannot be read at all

O7_producer.where: message.go:460-469 (attr.Value = b[:aL] aliases m.Raw and keeps the buffer's cap, so a value at the buffer end can have cap 0)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Drop the pre-read 'len(value) <= 4' guard from MappedAddress.GetFromAs so MAPPED-ADDRESS / ALTERNATE-SERVER / OTHER-ADDRESS / RESPONSE-ORIGIN panic the same way
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The two decoders are near-verbatim mirrors reading the family at the same offset (addr.go:75 vs xoraddr.go:94); the pinned tree already contains one written guard-first and one guard-last, so a maintainer refactoring either from the other will get the order wrong.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Move the fixed-offset reads value[2]/value[3] above the 'len(value) < 4' guard
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same shape - a length guard followed by fixed-offset reads of a m.Get value - and the guard/read order is the entire mechanism, so inverting it during a refactor looks harmless.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second decode entry that assigns m.Raw = data directly (tight cap) instead of append(m.Raw[:0], data...) as Decode/UnmarshalBinary do
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The library decoder aliases values into m.Raw (message.go:467), so any caller that sets Raw itself - the shipped CLI already does - makes cap == len reachable without touching the library.

O9_family: improper input validation: fixed-offset read of a length-unchecked attribute value (CWE-20)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Copy every attribute value out of the raw buffer inside Message.Decode (attr.Value = append([]byte(nil), b[:aL]...)) so no value can ever alias a tight buffer, which fixes the panic but silently breaks the documented zero-allocation contract and its benchmarks.
